_meta.purpose: Draft ledger for per-project manager-optimizer proposals (Phase 53, v1.2.0 centerpiece). DRAFT-ONLY: nothing reads this file to change any directive surface; no code path auto-applies a proposal, ever. Routing is fixed - target claude_manager drafts propose CLAUDE_MANAGER.md refinement text; target gate_config drafts propose gate-config.json key/value changes; never the other way.
_meta.written_by: manager-optimizer stages drafts as .claude/telemetry/optimizer-*.draft.json; sessionend-cost-proposals.sh folds staged drafts into the proposals array below at the SessionEnd seam (BATCH-AT-SEAMS). Humans edit status by hand after review.
_meta.apply_flow: Approved gate_config drafts are mechanical value edits the user asks CC to apply to .claude/gate-config.json. Approved claude_manager drafts are user-directed doc edits to CLAUDE_MANAGER.md. Either way, status flips to 'applied' only AFTER the edit has actually landed - 'approved' alone records a decision and triggers nothing.

entry_schema.timestamp: ISO 8601 UTC (when the finding was drafted)
entry_schema.finding: one-paragraph statement of the observed pattern
entry_schema.mechanical_evidence: array of strings - each line cites a file path plus a measured value (counts, timestamps, dollar estimates at named rates, commit ids). Model self-assessment is banned as an evidence source (see manager-optimizer / experiments/confidence/ANALYSIS.md).
entry_schema.draft: target claude_manager: concrete proposed directive text (quotable, placeable). target gate_config: concrete key/value change - existing keys or the documented-empty operation-tier/friction slots only (proposing values is in scope; defining new slots is not).
entry_schema.status: draft | approved | applied | rejected (human-edited; entries always ENTER as draft; 'applied' only after the edit lands)
entry_schema.review_note: optional, human-added at review: the rejection reason, or a note on the applied form (e.g. verbatim vs recalibrated per review direction)

_meta.runtime_state: .claude/telemetry/optimizer-state.json (gitignored, hook-created) carries {sessions_since_last_run, last_run_at, last_nudge_count}: the SessionEnd hook increments the counter, the SessionStart hook reads it for the cooldown-gated nudge line, and manager-optimizer resets it on dispatch.

proposals.finding: The per-session cost warn threshold (warn_usd_per_session=50.0) is below the measured cost of most real session rollups, so the warn fires on 9 of 13 data-carrying rollups (69%) and discriminates nothing. Session rollups in this install are multi-day cumulative lineages (resumed sessions re-emit cumulative counters under new ids), so 'per session' costs run far above a naive per-sitting expectation: median rollup $76.65, top four $334-$378 at the configured assumed_model rates. The 7-day threshold (250.0) is roughly calibrated against the true lineage delta ($216.07 measured 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-06) but any consumer that naively sums overlapping rollups will overcount that same window as $1,037.05 - a mechanism caveat noted here, not a threshold problem. Proposed: raise warn_usd_per_session to 200.0 so the warn flags the outlier tail (4 of 13 measured rollups) instead of the majority; leave warn_usd_per_7d unchanged.

proposals.finding: The codified dispatch discipline ('>5k tokens of context -> dispatch a helper'; 'more than three files end-to-end -> dispatch') is not being exercised: across seven weeks of telemetry the Agent tool fired 3 times out of 2,048 recorded tool events (0.15%), all agent:Explore within a 16-second span on 2026-05-19, while the manager performed 552 Bash / 412 Edit / 285 Read / 179 Write / 170 Grep events directly. The 11-helper roster the directive presents as the default path for multi-file work sees effectively zero interactive dispatch (hook-invoked producers like cruft-checker run as bash scripts and are not counted here). Either the heuristic's threshold is mis-calibrated for this install's meta-work, or direct-read is the de facto accepted norm and the directive overstates dispatch. The directive should carry the measured baseline so the divergence is visible and gets an explicit decision rather than silent drift.

proposals.finding: The observation-consumption directives in CLAUDE_MANAGER.md describe a producer mix and a triage flow that do not match the measured backlog. The directive names session-observer and task-watchdog as the two v1.1.0 producers; both have produced zero files. The actual backlog is 89% cruft-checker (135/152) plus session-end-telemetry (17/152). The workflow-suggester dispatch threshold ('~5-10 unreviewed patterns') has been crossed (16 unresolved as of 2026-07-06) with zero workflow-suggester dispatches ever recorded and zero captures ever drafted. The unresolved backlog itself is dominated by one deterministic false-positive class: 13 of 16 are broken-link findings against a single doc whose repo-root-relative link style resolves as missing from docs/. The directive should tell the manager to triage deterministic cruft backlogs by source and root cause in one pass, rather than route them toward a capture flow that has never fired.

That eight-day stretch was the Phase 57-75 governance arc plus the v1.1.5 cut - 58 commits of surgical known-anchor edits, zero reverts - which the reconciled rule legitimately routes to direct read, so the divergence is now consistent with the rule as written rather than silent drift. But the exploratory branch of the reconciled rule went completely unexercised in the window, so the rule's justification clause has never been tested. The directive section currently carries only the first-pass numbers; it should carry the second-pass measurement so the baseline stays current and the untested branch is named.

proposals.finding: The applied cycle-one triage directive (opt-20260707-observation-backlog-directive, status applied) worked for its target class: the cruft-checker backlog went from 16 unresolved at cycle one to 0 unresolved now, with a 16-observation batch resolution landing 2026-07-08 - one day after the paragraph was applied - including five observations that had sat 51.6 days. Every actionable producer is now at zero open files (cruft-checker 135/135 resolved, task-watchdog 3/3, roadmap-auditor 4/4 - the last resolved same-day, 10.3h after emission). The residue the directive did not cover is now 100% of the open backlog: all 21 unresolved observations are source session-end-telemetry, pattern_type token_telemetry - exactly one per session rollup file (21 rollups, 21 observations), occurrences always 1, oldest open since 2026-05-19 (58 days). These are per-session token records consumed by the cost surfaces, not defects; nothing in any flow ever flips their resolved_at. Counted against the '~5-10 unreviewed patterns' workflow-suggester threshold (operationalized as resolved_at null, per cycle one), they saturate it permanently - the threshold reads as crossed forever and grows by one per rollup checkpoint, muting the dispatch signal for every other producer.
